message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
I’ll give you both the **`gcloud` CLI** command (the easiest way) and the **REST API** payload you could use with `curl` or any HTTP client.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with the **Compute Engine API** enabled.  
> * You need a **GPU quota** for the zone you choose (e.g., `nvidia-tesla-a6000`).  
> * The **GPU API** (`compute.googleapis.com`) must be enabled.  
> * You must have the **Google Cloud SDK** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to suit your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pull the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Allows live migration during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the instance crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: run a shell script on first boot (e.g., install drivers). |
| `--tags` | Open HTTP/HTTPS ports (if you need them). |
| `--scopes` | Full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you want tighter security). |

> **Tip** – If you want to use a **custom machine type** (e.g., 16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM), replace `--machine-type` with `--custom-cpu=16 --custom-memory=64GB`.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (via `curl`)

Below is a **JSON payload** you can POST to the Compute Engine API.  
Replace the placeholders (`{project}`, `{zone}`, etc.) with your actual values.

```bash
# Set environment variables
export PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"
export INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON body – save this to a file or use it inline
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Explanation of the JSON fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (SSD, 100 GB, Ubuntu 20.04). |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Uses the default VPC and assigns an external IP. |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Attaches one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `scheduling` | Live‑migration enabled, automatic restart. |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script (installs NVIDIA driver). |

> **Note** – The `accessToken` is short‑lived; you can also use a service account key and `gcloud auth activate-service-account`.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE"

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 4. Optional: Using Terraform

If you prefer infrastructure as code, here’s a minimal Terraform snippet:

```hcl
provider "google" {
  project = "my-gcp-project"
  region  = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "rtx_a6000" {
  name         = "rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
  machine_type = "n1-standard-8"
  zone         = "us-central1-a"

  boot_disk {
    initialize_params {
      image = "ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      size  = 100
      type  = "pd-ssd"
    }
  }

  network_interface {
    network = "default"
    access_config {}
  }

  guest_accelerator {
    type  = "nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    count = 1
  }

  scheduling {
    on_host_maintenance = "MIGRATE"
    automatic_restart   = true
  }

  metadata_startup_script = <<-EOT
    #!/bin/bash
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
  EOT
}
```

Run `terraform init && terraform apply` to create the instance.

---

### Recap

| Step | Command / Tool | What it does |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| 1 | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, one‑liner CLI creation. |
| 2 | `curl … POST …` | Direct REST API call (useful for scripts). |
| 3 | `nvidia-smi` | Verify GPU inside the VM. |
| 4 | Terraform snippet | Declarative IaC approach. |

Pick the method that best fits your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
